question: I want one `dspy.Parallel` run to mix full `dspy.Example`s, plain keyword dictionaries, positional tuples, and even a nested concurrent sub-run. Which payload shapes are actually supported, and what special case makes the nested case work?
gold_answer: `dspy.Parallel` directly accepts `Example`, `dict`, and `tuple` payloads. It also accepts a `list`, but only for the special case where the callee's class name is exactly `Parallel`, which is how nested parallel sub-runs are routed. `Example`s are unpacked via `.inputs()`, dicts become keyword calls, tuples become positional calls, and other payload types raise `ValueError`.

rubric.statement: `Example` payloads are supported; in the `access_examples` path, `Parallel` invokes the callee with `module(**example.inputs())`.
`dict` payloads are supported and are forwarded as keyword arguments via `module(**example)`.
`tuple` payloads are supported and are forwarded as positional arguments via `module(*example)`.

`list` payloads are only accepted for the special nested case where the callee's class name is exactly `Parallel`; the nested test constructs `(self.parallel, [ ... ])` and expects that entry to return a nested sub-run result.
Any payload outside the supported `Example`/`dict`/`list`/`tuple` branches raises `ValueError`.
